name: Work → review → revise → review → revise → PR (2-judge gauntlet)
description: Package-agnostic code-review workflow — simplified. A coder agent does a task in a working directory, two INDEPENDENT reviewer agents critique it (B then C, each a fresh ephemeral session), the coder revises against each, and the final coder turn commits, pushes, and opens a PR. Pure acyclic DAG of 7 nodes: work → review_1 → anchor_check_1 → revise_1 → review_2 → anchor_check_2 → revise_2. The single coder session is --resumed across turns (carries its history v1→v2→v3); the two judges are distinct fresh sessions (generator≠evaluator + a second independent look at a revised draft). CODE DISCIPLINE: work/revise/review nodes inject skills/program_style.md (NSP) + skills/assert_on.md (assert-what-you-know) and prompt for fail-loud invariants over silent fallbacks; reviewers may REJECT on discipline failures with file:line. CITATION GUARD: review:anchor-check nodes sit between each review→revise edge; they resolve plain file:line citations in reviewer output against the cwd and annotate unresolvable ones with [UNVERIFIED CITATION: ...] before the coder revises against them — hallucinated file:line no longer burns a coder turn. Full receipt tokens (path:Lx@commit#hash) are left to the safe-commit gate. revise_2 ALWAYS commits, pushes, and opens a PR — no gating. Callable by id from ANY chat or cartridge: POST /workflow {workflowId:"review-gauntlet", params:{task, cwd}} (or save a preset). NOT zohar-specific — zohar is just one caller (its drift fix = a task that says 'edit only this doc to match the code'). Params: task (the work to do, with all specifics baked in), cwd (a git worktree/branch the CALLER prepared off its chosen base — lifecycle is the caller's so cleanup-on-failure is guaranteed in imperative code, and 'branch off origin/main' stays a caller policy, not baked in). The PR URL is the terminal output.

params.prompt:
You are completing a task in THIS directory — an isolated git worktree, so editing files here is safe and cannot affect anyone else's work.

=== TASK ===
{{params.task}}


=== CODE DISCIPLINE (mandatory — skills/program_style.md + skills/assert_on.md) ===
You write and revise under Negative Space Programming (NSP) + Assert What You Know:
- System BOUNDARIES (user input, external APIs, deserialization, untrusted HTTP): stay defensive.
- INSIDE those boundaries: assert load-bearing invariants; do NOT paper over them with ?? defaults, silent coercions, optional chaining on known-present values, or try/catch around "shouldn't throw".
- Assert at point of use with a message that states WHY the invariant is true (precondition source), not just that a value is "required".
- Prefer loud, precise failure over silent wrong success (empty placeholders, ignored isError, fallbacks that hide bugs).
- Real race/edge cases: handle defensively AND document why; speculative guards: remove.
- No .catch(() => {}); log or bound. Repeated guards → extract assertX().
- Surface assumptions before coding; only assert what is load-bearing and flow-guaranteed.
- Surgical edits: only lines that serve the task; match existing style.
Read the injected skill docs if present; if a change would violate NSP, fix the design rather than adding a soft fallback.

Complete the task now by editing files in this directory. Do NOT commit, push, or open a pull request yet — just make the changes. When you are done, reply with a short summary of what you changed and why, including any invariants you asserted (and why they hold).

meta.description: Coder A, fresh session. Does the task in cwd under NSP + assert-what-you-know (skills injected); returns session id for --resume.

params.prompt:
You are an independent, adversarial reviewer (reviewer B), scoped to THIS directory. Another agent just attempted this task:

=== TASK ===
{{params.task}}

Read the ACTUAL files in this directory and judge whether the work correctly and completely satisfies the task. Be specific and skeptical.

=== CODE DISCIPLINE REVIEW (mandatory — skills/program_style.md + skills/assert_on.md) ===
In addition to task completeness, REJECT for discipline failures when they are real and concrete:
- Hidden assumptions: ?? / "should always be set" null guards / ?. on invariant paths that should be assert
- Silent wrong success: empty placeholders as ok, ignored isError/error flags, swallowed .catch(() => {})
- Defensive code for impossible cases inside the system (should assert or redesign)
- Assertion messages that only say "required" without WHY / precondition source
- Speculative try/catch or fallbacks with no evidence of a real edge case
- Real races handled with bare throw-and-hope instead of documented defensive handling
APPROVE only if the task is satisfied AND the change does not introduce the above. Cite file:line for each discipline issue.

Your reply MUST BEGIN with exactly one token: APPROVE or REJECT.
- APPROVE only if the work genuinely and completely satisfies the task AND passes the code-discipline bar above.
- If REJECT, list each concrete problem (task or discipline), the file it is in, and exactly what must change.

meta.description: Judge B — FRESH session. Task completeness + NSP/assert discipline bar; leads with APPROVE/REJECT.
Validate reviewer B's file:line citations against cwd. Unresolvable citations get [UNVERIFIED CITATION: ...] annotation. Passes text through unchanged when no citations or on resolver failure.

If the reviewer APPROVED with nothing to change, leave the work as-is. Otherwise re-read the relevant files and address EVERY point the reviewer raised (task gaps AND code-discipline issues). Prefer asserts with WHY-messages over soft fallbacks. Do NOT commit, push, or open a PR yet. Reply with a short summary of what you changed in response.

After addressing all points from reviewer C, COMMIT, PUSH, and OPEN A PULL REQUEST:
1. Check what you changed: git status --short
2. Land it — the ONLY approved path (mention asserted invariants or fail-loud honesty in the message if that was the point of the task):
   bash $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/agentruntime/scripts/ship-guard.sh -m 'conventional message' <each changed path>
   It refuses to push main/master, refuses to ship from the shared main checkout, and takes explicit paths only (there is no -A — a shared-index sweep steals other agents' in-flight work). If it REFUSES, STOP and report its message verbatim; do not route around it with raw git.
3. Open a pull request against main with a summary of the change, both reviews, and any NSP/assert discipline fixes.

Reply with the resulting pull-request URL on a single line. If nothing changed and there is nothing to ship, reply exactly: NO-CHANGES.
